0.content:
Jean is Barbara's older sister. When their parents separated, Jean stayed with their mother Frederica and was trained as the Gunnhildr heir; Barbara stayed with their father. Jean has always wanted to get closer but cannot find the words when Barbara's eyes slide away, and Barbara behaves the same way. Barbara tried all her life to beat Jean at one thing, whether swords or grades, and never managed it. She still admires her and wishes she could lighten her load. Jean thinks Barbara is "too hard on herself", and knows it because the Knights also oversee the Church.

Barbara nursed Jean after she collapsed from overwork in Jean's story quest (1.0) and knew, a little too well for a mere colleague, that Jean goes to Vennessa's tree at Windrise when she feels lost. In a 2022 birthday letter Barbara says she asked Jean for advice about a plateau, and Jean told her to persevere: growth is accumulation. In the Durin crisis (5.6), Jean warned Barbara privately before the attacks; Barbara's only question was who would protect Jean. In the Windblume event (1.4, limited) Barbara briefly feared the "precious thing" stolen from her was Jean. The Summertime Sparkle outfit text puts her wish plainly: give me my sister back, just for a while.

1.comment: Barbara: Seamus Pegg and Frederica Gunnhildr
1.content:
Barbara's father Seamus Pegg was once a famous adventurer who started over in Mondstadt's Church and rose to Seneschal, known as the Cardinal of Daybreak. He raised Barbara, was surprised by her determination, and counselled her to become a healer. Her mother Frederica Gunnhildr is a veteran knight of the Gunnhildr Clan who raised Jean. Both parents left with Grand Master Varka's expedition; Seamus handed his Church duties to Cardinal Calvin, and Barbara has prayed for their safe return.

Frederica was sent back to defend Dornman Port; on the eve of Jean's 2025 birthday she and Barbara surprised Jean at Knights headquarters. Seamus returned after the Nod-Krai crisis. In early 2026 Barbara threw herself into preparing the Cathedral for "the Cardinal's" homecoming, even planning a new hymn.

2.comment: Barbara: Alice and the Idol Magazine
2.content:
Barbara first heard the word "idol" from Alice, an elder of the Hexenzirkel. Confused that anyone but The Seven could be worshipped, she was handed an "Idol Magazine" from some unknown world and learned that idols work hard to be liked and can heal people's spirits through song and dance. She threw herself into learning songs and found happiness in others' smiles. When Alice's plans for "Teyvat Idols!" collapsed, Barbara decided she would define what an idol is herself. She repeats Alice's maxim that a true idol tries to heal the souls of the people.

Dahlia suspects the idol project became a "genius marketing move" for the Church, filling the pews, though he doubts Barbara or Alice planned it that way. Dahlia's own character story notes that before then, only a Barbara concert could pack the Cathedral.

3.comment: Barbara: Venti and the Holy Lyre
3.content:
At the end of the Prologue (1.0) Barbara came to collect the Holy Lyre der Himmel, the Church relic the Traveler and Venti had borrowed. Its broken state made her scream and swear that a lifetime of penance would not be enough. Venti quietly "repaired" it with Anemo, and she snatched it back, forbidding them ever to touch it again. Minutes later she found the Traveler unconscious outside the Cathedral after Signora's attack and healed them. Her powers had almost no effect on Venti, who called it "completely normal" and left for Windrise.

The repair was an illusion. In 1.4 Paimon notes she still has not realised, and in her Hangout Event Barbara praises the bard's magic while noticing the Traveler's nervous face. She admires Venti's voice but finds his melodies too complicated to learn. She once sang an impromptu duet with him at a Knights charity sale, where he sang a harmony to guide her in.

4.content:
Rosaria is the Church's most absent sister, and Barbara is the one person who keeps trying to reach her: reminding her not to smoke in the Cathedral, chasing her to services and choir practice. Rosaria calls her a thorn in her side and suspects Victoria set Barbara to watch her. Barbara admits she has not quite found the courage to really talk to her, and insists Rosaria surely believes in the Anemo Archon.

In 1.2 Barbara tracked Rosaria all the way to Dragonspine to bring her to a commemorative choir event; Rosaria told her she was too trusting and sent her hurrying back. In the 1.4 Windblume event (limited), Rosaria overheard Barbara's panic over a missing Bennett and pointed the group to the Thousand Winds Temple. During the Durin crisis (5.6) Rosaria told her that doing what she is good at is more than enough, then escorted the wounded and left the Cathedral in Barbara's hands. Rosaria once suggested a different way to calm crying children, and the story of the brave Honorary Knight worked wonders.

5.content:
Dahlia is a fellow deacon. Barbara looks up to him because he brings the word of Barbatos to the clergy, and notes he is hard to find, preferring markets and taverns to the quiet Cathedral. Dahlia calls her a friend who is always there to support him, and deliberately asks her for help because helping makes her happiest. It was Dahlia who once had Barbara fetch Rosaria for choir practice.

In 6.5 Dahlia chatted with Barbara outside the Cathedral about her new hymn and assured her that Venti rates her songs above fine wine. In confession he admitted lying to her by hiding that Venti is Barbatos, after she had rejected the truth once already.

6.comment: Barbara: Bennett and the Adhesive Bandages
6.content:
Bennett is at the Cathedral so often with fractures and dislocations that even Barbara is surprised at how skilled he has become at popping joints back in. She tells him he should take better care of himself. When he apologises ("Sorry, it's me again..."), she shakes her head and tosses him adhesive bandages "for those scratches as well". Bennett treasures them like medals. He goes to her concerts after bad adventures and envies her popularity.

The Traveler heard that Albert, leader of her fan club, would get himself bruised to visit the Cathedral, only to find a month later that Bennett saw her far more often. In the 1.4 Windblume event (limited) Bennett was with her when the "threat" letter arrived, rushed off to the Thousand Winds Temple he recognised from its map, and went missing there.

7.comment: Barbara: The Barbara Fan Club and Sister Victoria
7.content:
Albert, a citizen who lingers at the Cathedral doors, leads the Barbara Fan Club, "the biggest club for Barbara-sama fans in all of Mondstadt". The nuns keep chasing him off; the senior nun Victoria distrusts him without knowing he is only a fan. Barbara once scolded him for humming her songs out of tune. Victoria, who listens to confessions and watches over the younger clergy, makes Barbara report where she is going so the Church can rescue her from crowds, and wishes she would stop overworking.

In the Hangout Event (1.4) Barbara hid from Albert in Wolvendom, then felt guilty when it turned out he had come to bring her the red Wolfhook berries she needed. Victoria told the Traveler that cleaning is Barbara's job and that she always insists on doing it alone.

8.comment: Barbara: Hangout Event - Wellspring of Healing
8.content: Barbara's Hangout Event (1.4) begins with Sister Victoria worried because Barbara has not returned from herb-picking. The Traveler finds her in Wolvendom looking for red Wolfhooks for the Dawn Winery worker Tunner's cough. She hides from her fans and admits she came partly for a rare quiet afternoon. She explains that she joined the Church because her father always worked there and to learn to truly heal, since singing alone could not. Later she offers the Traveler either the Cat's Tail's new "Fantastic Summer-Serendipity Coral Sparkling Tea" or her own Chilibrew. One path ends with her mobbed by fans at the tavern. Another sees her secretly trailing Treasure Hoarders to rescue a kidnapped merchant. A third has her heal Uwe, a Treasure Hoarder who had been feigning injury and then was really hurt; she treats him anyway, and he swears no Treasure Hoarder will touch her again.

9.comment: Barbara: The Durin Crisis at the Cathedral
9.content: In Paralogism (5.6), when mimics from the dragon Durin's remains attacked Mondstadt, Barbara stayed at the Cathedral treating wounded knights such as Swan and keeping a full injury record. Jean had warned her days before, on Albedo's word, and asked her to take care of herself; Barbara asked who would protect Jean. She told Rosaria she had to do her part, trusted that Jean and the others had prepared well, and afterwards reported happily that injuries were few. She appears again in the closing cutscene of The Gardener.
